items.title: The Woman at the Well
items.body:
I want to start by saying welcome to Chosen; we are so glad you are here.

To give a little context and background to John 4 and the story of the woman at the well: we learn that Jesus was leaving Judea because the Pharisees were upset that He was making and baptizing more disciples than John. Knowing this, Jesus left Judea and headed toward Galilee.

In order to reach Galilee by the quickest route, He would have to pass through Samaria. To many Jews, Samaria and its people were considered unclean, and they would often bypass the region entirely. But in John 4:4, Scripture says, “He had to pass through Samaria.”
Jesus could have gone around but He chose to journey through. Some commentaries suggest He may have been divinely directed to take this route. Either way, the path was intentional.

Jesus arrives in Samaria, weary from His journey, and sits at the town well around the sixth hour about noon in the heat of the day. I don’t know about you, but I run from the heat!! This was not the optimal time to draw water. Water was typically drawn in the morning or evening when it was cooler.

This is when we are introduced to a woman who came at this unusual hour, likely seeking to be alone. Yet when she arrived, she was not alone. She met Jesus.
He speaks to her and asks her for water a request that breaks cultural and social norms. A Jewish man speaking publicly to a Samaritan woman was unheard of. Then Jesus offers her “living water,” speaking of the Holy Spirit dwelling within her. She misunderstands at first and takes Him literally.

Jesus then gently exposes her situation, revealing that He knows her story. Through this moment, He reveals Himself to her as the Messiah "Anointed/Chosen One" (John 4:26).

I chose this narrative because it aligns so closely with the heart behind Chosen Collective & Co. This entire story is about being chosen.

Jesus could have walked around Samaria but the path was chosen. And that path led Him directly to a woman in need of the living water only He could provide.

She chose to go to the well at a time she thought would be empty. He chose to meet her there.
A Jew who “should have had no dealings” with a Samaritan and a woman at that chose to reveal Himself to her. In fact, this is the first time in Scripture where Jesus explicitly declares, “I who speak to you am He.”

And what was the first thing she chose to do?
She ran and told others about Him.
He knew her name.
He knew her story.
He was never concerned with social approval.
He was a master at relational connection.
He chose her.
He chooses you.

He chose to extend His grace through Jesus. He is seeking you and the cross proves that.
She came thirsty. And it is in our nature to thirst.
But it is only in His nature to truly satisfy.

So the question becomes:
What are you drinking from?
What are you thirsting for?
What are you longing for?
What are you looking to for satisfaction?

Lord, forgive us when we choose to drink from things that are not flowing from You — things that do not please You and expect them to satisfy us when You are who we truly long for.

Verses to carry with you this week:
John 4:26
1 Peter 2:9
